title: The Moser–Tardos theorem (algorithmic Lovász Local Lemma)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Moser–Tardos theorem in the variable setting: finitely many independent random variables with finite ranges, n events each determined by a finite set of variables, neighbours sharing a variable. If P(A_j) ≤ x_j ∏_{k ∈ Γ(j)} (1 − x_k) with 0 ≤ x_j < 1, the resampling algorithm (always resampling the first violated event), run on a random resampling table, resamples A_j at most x_j / (1 − x_j) times in expectation among its first t steps, for every t; the expected total number of resamplings is at most ∑_j x_j / (1 − x_j); the probability that it has not stopped after t steps is at most (∑_j x_j / (1 − x_j)) / t; and some assignment avoids all events (the Lovász Local Lemma in the variable setting). The proof formalizes witness trees built from the log, the τ-check coupling with the resampling table, and the Galton–Watson bound.
